Subject: AcmeHealth private VPC dataflow - follow-up on PII & egress controls

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our call with your security and infra teams:

Summary of ask:
- You plan to run Redwood in a Private/VPC deployment inside AcmeHealth (VPC peering or S2S VPN).
- Primary concerns: PII/PHI handling, data retention and deletion policies, request/response logging controls, and strict egress restrictions (no internet outbound from processing subnets).

Immediate clarifications we promised to follow up on:
1) Data types: confirm whether PII includes full patient records, free-text notes, and attachments (you mentioned identifiers + notes).
2) Retention: your retention/archival requirements (accessible period vs long-term archive).
3) Logging: what level of request/response logging is permitted/required for audit vs what must be redacted or omitted.
4) Egress: clarify exact egress rules (allowed destination IP ranges, whether model downloads/patching can be scheduled via an approved egress path).

Attached: dataflow diagram from today’s whiteboard and a short SOC 2 summary about our controls.

Next steps suggested:
- Can we get answers to 1-4 above by end of day Thursday?
- Schedule a technical architecture deep-dive next week (I’m proposing Wed 9/15 10:00 AM PT) with Dev (Dev Patel), Security (Neha Kapoor), and your infra lead.
- If helpful, we can provide an internal note describing options for egress (customer NAT egress, static IPs, S2S VPN, or air-gapped bundles).

Thanks — we want to make sure we map a design that fits your compliance constraints.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth private VPC dataflow - follow-up on PII & egress controls

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side inline: 

On data types: we will be sending patient identifiers (name, MRN), clinically sensitive free-text (progress notes, clinical summaries), and small binary attachments (images). For privacy categorization, please treat anything that can identify a patient as PII/PHI.

Retention: our legal team requires that data used for inference remain accessible for 90 days. After that, it should be archived for 7 years in our long-term archive (encrypted). We cannot keep full request/response pairs beyond 90 days unless redacted.

Logging: audit logs for access and inference requests are required. However, request/response payload storage of full PHI must be avoided. If you retain logs for telemetry, they must be redacted or masked such that PHI elements are removed. We will need a controls description for how Redwood can support redaction or pseudonymization prior to storage.

Egress: critical constraint — processing subnets in our VPC cannot have general internet egress. Outbound traffic must be limited to our approved destination IP ranges (we will share a list) and to specific services (e.g., our telemetry/observability collector).
- Model updates: acceptable if delivered via an approved staging bucket accessible over the S2S VPN or by exchanging offline model bundles via our secure file transfer process.

Can you provide an updated dataflow diagram that explicitly shows network boundaries, which subnets will have outbound blocked, and where logs will be stored/encrypted? Procurement is looped in for contract/security artifacts (NDA + DSAs).

Thanks — Sam
Samantha Green
Director, Security & Privacy
AcmeHealth

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for the detail. A few technical notes from our side on how Redwood Private can be configured to meet these constraints: 

1) Deployment options:
- Private control plane with customer-managed VPC peering or site-to-site VPN.
- On-prem / air-gapped option available where we package model bundles and updates; operator performs offline install.

2) Egress controls:
- We can operate with zero general outbound egress from processing subnets. Typical patterns we support:
  * Customer NAT gateway with static egress IPs that we allowlist for any required outbound destinations.
  * Site-to-site VPN to your telemetry/observability endpoints so metrics and health checks terminate inside your environment.
  * Offline model update process for air-gapped setups — we deliver model bundles to your secure bucket or SFTP endpoint.

3) Logging & PHI:
- By default, request/response payloads are not persisted beyond the serving node unless configured. We support local ephemeral logging (for live debugging) and configurable redaction hooks before logs are forwarded to any long-term storage.
- Options: upstream redaction filter (your side) or a Redwood-side redaction/pseudonymization plugin that strips PHI fields before storing. We can share a sample plugin and guidance.

4) Encryption & key management:
- Data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed KMS (customer-supplied keys) in Dedicated/Private installs.

Action items for us:
- I’ll produce an updated dataflow diagram that shows VPC subnets, processing nodes, and exact egress control points and circulate before Friday.
- Can you confirm the IP ranges and the list of acceptable destinations (or whether S2S VPN is preferred)?

Link: internal networking note (design doc) - https://drive.google.com/example/acmehealth-private-vpc-design

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Infra
Redwood Inference
